{{More footnotes|date=September 2025}}

In mathematical [[harmonic analysis|abstract harmonic analysis]], '''Harish-Chandra's Schwartz space''' is a space of functions on a [[semisimple Lie group]] whose derivatives are rapidly decreasing, studied by [[Harish-Chandra]].<ref name="Harish-Chandra">{{Citation | last1=Harish-Chandra | title=Discrete series for semisimple Lie groups. II. Explicit determination of the characters | doi=10.1007/BF02392813 |mr=0219666 | year=1966 | journal=[[Acta Mathematica]] | issn=0001-5962 | volume=116 | pages=1–111| s2cid=125806386 | url=http://projecteuclid.org/euclid.acta/1485889477 | doi-access=free }}</ref> It is an analogue of the [[Schwartz space]] on a real [[vector space]], and is used to define the space of [[tempered representation|tempered distributions]] on a semisimple [[Lie group]].

== Prerequisites ==
=== Length functions ===
Let <math>G</math> be a topological group. A length on <math>G</math> is a continuous function <math>l: G \mapsto [0, +\infty[</math>, such that for all <math>g, g' \in G</math>, <math>l(gg') \leq l(g) + l(g')</math>.<ref name="vlafforgue">{{Citation | last1=V. Lafforgue | title=K-théorie bivariante pour les algèbres de Banach et conjecture de Baum-Connes | doi=10.1007/s002220200213 | year=2002 | journal=[[Inventiones mathematicae]] | url=https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s002220200213.pdf | doi-access=free }}</ref> These functions are used to define spaces with rapidly decreasing functions on locally compact topological groups, since they are used to define polynomial weights  to ensure rapid decay.<ref name="Harish-Chandra"/><ref name="vlafforgue"/>

=== The <math> \sigma </math> function ===
Let <math>G</math> be a semisimple connected Lie group with Lie algebra <math>\mathfrak{g}</math>, and let <math>K</math> be its [[maximal compact subgroup]]. Then, the [[Cartan decomposition]] of <math>G</math> allows one to state that the mapping 
<math>
(k, X) \mapsto k \exp(X)
</math>
,<math>k \in K</math> and <math>X \in \mathfrak{p}</math> is an analytic diffeomorphism of <math>K \times \mathfrak{p} </math> onto <math> G </math>.<br/> Let <math>b</math> be the [[Killing form]] of <math>\mathfrak{g}</math>. Its restriction on <math>\mathfrak{p}</math> provides an euclidean norm <math>\| X \|</math>, <math>K</math>-invariant, and such that <math>\langle Z, (adZ)^2Y \rangle = \langle (ad Z)^2X, Y \rangle</math> for all <math>X, Y, Z \in \mathfrak{p} </math>, where <math>\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle </math> is the inner product corresponding to <math>\| \cdot \|</math>.<br/> The <math> \sigma </math> function of <math>G</math> is then defined as <math> \sigma(x) = \| X \| </math> for <math>x = k \exp(X)</math>.<ref name="Harish-Chandra"/> It is proved <ref name="Harish-Chandra"/> that <math>\sigma</math> is a length function. Of course, <math>\sigma</math> is equal to <math>0</math> on <math>K</math>, and for all <math>x \in G</math>, <math>\sigma(x^{-1}) = \sigma(x)</math>.<ref name="Harish-Chandra"/>

==Definition==

In order to define the Harish-Chandra Schwartz space on a semisimple Lie group <math>G</math>, one uses the [[Harish-Chandra's Ξ function]] and the <math>\sigma</math> function of <math>G</math>, defined in the former section.
The Schwartz space on <math>G</math> consists roughly of the functions all of whose derivatives are rapidly decreasing compared to&nbsp;''Ξ''. More precisely, let's suppose <math>G</math> is connected, and let's define <math>\nu_{r, g_1, g_2}(f) = \displaystyle \sup_{g \in G}{| g_1 \ast f(g) \ast g_2 | \Xi^{-1}(g)(1+\sigma(g))^r}</math> for all <math>r \in \mathbb{R}</math>, where <math>g_1</math> and <math>g_2</math> belong to the [[universal enveloping algebra]] <math>U \mathfrak{g}</math> of <math>\mathfrak{g}</math>, <math>\ast</math> denotes its action on <math>G</math> as differential operators,<ref name="diff_op">{{Citation | last1=Helgason | title=Integral Geometry and Radon Transforms | doi=10.1007/978-1-4419-6055-9_9 | year= 2010 | journal=[[Springer Nature|Springer]] | url=https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-1-4419-6055-9_9 | doi-access=free | url-access=subscription }}</ref> and <math>r \in \mathbb{R}</math>. <br/> 
The Harish-Chandra Schwartz space is defined as the subspace <math>S(G)</math> of <math>\mathcal{C}^\infty(G)</math> such that <math>f \in S(G)</math> if and only if <math>\nu_{r, g_1, g_2}(f) < +\infty</math> for every <math>g_1, g_2 \in U \mathfrak{g}</math>, <math>r \in \mathbb{R}</math>. Topologized with the set of such seminorms, it is a [[Fréchet space]]. Since <math>G</math> is connected, the set of smooth functions with compact support <math>\mathcal{C}_c^\infty(G)</math> on <math>G</math> is dense in <math>S(G)</math>.<ref name="Harish-Chandra"/>
